title: Magic Methods
learning_outcomes: Explain what magic methods contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: __get() and __set().
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Advanced object design is about collaboration and stable contracts. Interfaces, composition, dependency injection, namespaces, and autoloading help change or test parts independently. In this lesson, focus on __get() and __set(); then compare it with __call() and __callstatic(). Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use magic methods when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Advanced object design is about collaboration and stable contracts. Interfaces, composition, dependency injection, namespaces, and autoloading help change or test parts independently. For magic methods, begin with __get() and __set(). Also distinguish __call() and __callstatic(); __tostring(); __invoke(). Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for magic methods from top to bottom. Start by identifying __get() and __set(), write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
